home.name: Jeremy Swayman
home.news: Swayman will start vs. Winnipeg on Wednesday.

home.name: Jacob Markstrom
home.news: Markstrom has had an up-and-down return to Florida, battling adversity in recent games, but he still managed a 4-3 win in his most recent game, despite allowing three goals on 19 shots (.842 SV%) against the Buffalo Sabres. The 36-year-old Swedish goalie has allowed three or more goals in five of seven November games (4-3-0), posting a pedestrian .892 SV%. The Panthers enter Wednesday's game as -117 home favourites against the red-hot Ottawa Senators, who have points in nine straight games (7-0-2).

home.name: Ilya Sorokin
home.news: After establishing himself as an elite goalie in his first three seasons, Sorokin has posted mid-pack statistics for three consecutive seasons. The 31-year-old goalie is off to a strong start in 2026-27, performing better under new Head Coach Pete DeBoer, but he suffered a 4-2 loss in his most recent outing, allowing three goals on 31 shots (.903 SV%) against the Toronto Maple Leafs. In November, Sorokin has a 2.47 GAA and .925 SV% in six games (3-1-2). The Islanders enter Wednesday's game as -117 home favourites against the St. Louis Blues, who have won four straight games.

away.name: Dustin Wolf
away.news: Wolf will start in Pittsburgh on Wednesday.

away.name: Joseph Woll
away.news: Woll will start in Washington on Wednesday.

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Over the past two seasons, Thompson quietly became one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. That said, the 29-year-old goalie has been flat-out unreliable through the quarter-mark of the 2026-27 season. In his most recent outing, Thompson didn't even last a full period, allowing three goals on five shots (.400 SV%) in an eventual 6-3 loss to the Buffalo Sabres. He has allowed three or more goals in all but five of 15 games this season (7-6-0). The Capitals enter Wednesday's game as -152 home favourites against a Philadelphia Flyers team on a three-game winning streak.

home.name: Daniil Tarasov
home.news: Tarasov has unexpectedly been getting more playing time in recent weeks, emerging as one of the NHL's most consistent goalies this season. That said, the 27-year-old goalie is coming off a 4-1 loss to the Boston Bruins, allowing three goals on 30 shots (.900 SV%). He hasn't received much goal support, as evidenced by a 1-4-0 record in his last five games, but he has an impressive 2.21 GAA and .927 SV% in those games.
